      "mainEntity": [
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "When does an older switchboard need repair or replacement?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Condition, faults, the existing protection and proposed electrical work guide that decision. An older board needs professional assessment, not an automatic full-replacement claim based on age alone."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Can I get an itemised quote before approving an upgrade?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Yes. The written scope identifies the proposed equipment and work, testing, any supply coordination and additional work requiring approval. Confirm inclusions before proceeding."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "How much does a switchboard upgrade cost in Perth?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Cost depends on the assessed installation, equipment, circuit work, access and supply arrangements. We quote for that scope; no single price is assumed to cover every board or property."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Will a switchboard upgrade fix a circuit that keeps tripping?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Not necessarily. The cause may lie in connected equipment or a circuit. Investigation should establish the fault before an upgrade is presented as the solution."
          }
        }
      ]

tap-mixer-repairs-perth.html.description: Tap and mixer repairs in Perth for dripping, leaking or faulty kitchen, bathroom and laundry fittings. Book an assessment and written repair quote.

faq.question: Does a dripping mixer always need replacing?
faq.answer: No. The cause, fitting condition and availability of compatible parts need assessment. Ask the quote to distinguish a repair from product supply and installation if replacement is recommended.

faq.question: Can I supply the replacement mixer myself?
faq.answer: Discuss the product and existing connections first. Dimensions, mounting and compatibility can affect installation. The quote should identify who supplies the fitting and whether additional connection work is required.

faq.question: Why does a tap keep dripping after it is turned off?
faq.answer: A worn seal or fitting fault can let water pass after shut-off; an outlet drip and base leak need different checks. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Can a dripping tap waste water over time?
faq.answer: Yes. Continued dripping wastes water; the amount depends on the actual rate and how long it continues. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Can I supply my own replacement mixer tap?
faq.answer: Yes, if the selected mixer suits the installation. Confirm compatibility and the installation inclusions before buying. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Do I need to diagnose the problem first?
faq.answer: No. Describe the observable change and property context. We inspect the affected area on site to establish the cause and confirm the repair scope. If more access is needed, we agree it with you first.

faq.question: Can I send photos?
faq.answer: Photos are optional: email safely taken photos to maxinemaintenance.au@outlook.com. You can contact us without photos. Do not approach a hazard, remove covers or dismantle equipment to take a photo.

faq.question: Can you help with a dripping tap?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us the fixture location, whether it drips constantly and any other changes you have noticed.

faq.question: Should I try to dismantle a mixer?
faq.answer: No. It is safer to describe the problem and leave the fitting intact for assessment.

faq.question: Do you work on rental-property fixtures?
faq.answer: Yes. Property managers can include work-order and access details.

faq.question: Can you install a tap I have already purchased?
faq.answer: We assess the product specifications, mounting arrangement and connection compatibility before agreeing the installation. Tell us whether product supply or installation only is required so the written quote covers the right scope.

toilet-installation-perth.html.description: Toilet installation and replacement in Perth with agreed supply, removal and taking away. Check fit, water and waste connections before quoting.

headings.text: Common situations and what to report
Replacing a toilet rather than a cistern part
Checking the proposed suite before ordering
Assessment, work plan and written quote

faq.question: Do you supply the toilet and remove the old one?
faq.answer: Yes. The agreed installation package includes the selected toilet, removal and taking away the old unit. The written quote identifies the product and any additional connection or access work.

faq.question: Can a running toilet be repaired without replacing the whole toilet?
faq.answer: Often the fault needs assessment of cistern components rather than an immediate new suite. We explain the findings and available repair or replacement scope before you approve the work.

faq.question: Does a blocked toilet mean I need a new toilet?
faq.answer: No. A blockage, a cistern fault and a damaged toilet suite are different problems. Drainage needs assessment where water backs up or other outlets are affected; replacing a suite does not automatically clear a downstream blockage.

faq.question: Should I book toilet repairs or drain clearing for a backed-up bowl?
faq.answer: Explain whether the water rises when flushed and whether other outlets are affected. The drainage page is the starting point for backups; the toilet repair page covers cistern, fill, flush and fitting faults. The assessment confirms the actual work.

faq.question: Is a complete new toilet needed when the cistern keeps running?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The fixture condition and repair parts need assessment first. If replacement is proposed, confirm the product, connections and any additional work in the written scope.

faq.question: What is the difference between a running toilet and a leaking toilet base?
faq.answer: A running cistern passes or replenishes water internally; a base leak is external water with a source that needs checking. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Why does my toilet keep refilling on its own?
faq.answer: Unwanted water loss from the cistern can trigger refilling. Inspection determines which component, if any, needs repair. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Do I need to diagnose the problem first?
faq.answer: No. Describe the observable change and property context. We inspect the affected area on site to establish the cause and confirm the repair scope. If more access is needed, we agree it with you first.

faq.question: Can I send photos?
faq.answer: Photos are optional: email safely taken photos to maxinemaintenance.au@outlook.com. You can contact us without photos. Do not approach a hazard, remove covers or dismantle equipment to take a photo.

faq.question: What if the toilet is running constantly?
faq.answer: Tell us whether it is continuously running, whether there is water on the floor and whether the fixture can still be used.

faq.question: What should I do if it is overflowing?
faq.answer: Avoid further use and keep people away from contaminated water. Contact us with the property details and the situation.

faq.question: Could a blocked toilet involve other drains?
faq.answer: Tell us if another fixture is also slow, gurgling or backing up. That context helps distinguish a toilet-specific concern from a broader drainage issue.

faq.question: Can you help with multiple toilets at one property?
faq.answer: Yes. Identify each affected fixture and its symptoms in the enquiry.

faq.question: Does every running toilet need to be replaced?
faq.answer: No. We assess the component fault, condition and availability of compatible parts. A complete replacement is a separate option with its own installation requirements and written scope.

faq.question: Can you guarantee finding a hidden leak without opening a wall?
faq.answer: Access and the suspected source determine what investigation is appropriate. Do not assume that every leak can be located or repaired without opening finishes. The proposed method and any access or restoration work need to be explained before approval.

faq.question: Does a high water bill prove there is a leaking pipe?
faq.answer: No. It is useful context, not a diagnosis. Include any observed water, changes in use and available records. If the concern is at the water meter or supply network, use Water Corporation guidance rather than assuming it is private pipework.

faq.question: Can a hidden water leak cause a high bill without visible water damage?
faq.answer: Yes, a concealed leak is possible without visible damage. A bill increase alone is insufficient to diagnose one. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Why is my water meter moving when no water is being used?
faq.answer: Flow without expected use can indicate a leak or a fixture still drawing water. It cannot locate the source. Read the explanation.

faq.question: Do I need to diagnose the problem first?
faq.answer: No. Describe the observable change and property context. We inspect the affected area on site to establish the cause and confirm the repair scope. If more access is needed, we agree it with you first.

faq.question: Can I send photos?
faq.answer: Photos are optional: email safely taken photos to maxinemaintenance.au@outlook.com. You can contact us without photos. Do not approach a hazard, remove covers or dismantle equipment to take a photo.

faq.question: Can you help with a hidden water leak?
faq.answer: Yes. Describe the property area, any visible moisture and changes you have noticed. This helps us understand the request before work is arranged.

faq.question: What should I include in a leak enquiry?
faq.answer: Include the address, affected room or outdoor area, when the issue began, whether water is active and any safe photos.

faq.question: What if water is near electrical equipment?
faq.answer: Keep clear of the area and do not touch wet electrical equipment. If there is immediate danger, move to safety and call 000.

faq.question: Are locating the leak and repairing it the same job?
faq.answer: They can be separate parts of the scope. We explain the investigation, access and proposed repair before work proceeds, and identify any additional access or reinstatement work in the written quote.

faq.question: What causes water hammer in household pipes?
faq.answer: A sudden change in water flow can create a pressure surge and a banging sound. Pipe support, valves and the installation may contribute. A plumber assesses the pattern and system before specifying the appropriate work.

faq.question: Can low water pressure be a public supply issue?
faq.answer: Yes. A property-wide change may involve supply conditions as well as private plumbing. Check Water Corporation notices, particularly if neighbours are affected. A single slow outlet is a different starting point for investigation.

faq.question: Can you investigate low water pressure throughout the house?
faq.answer: Yes. Report which outlets are affected, whether hot and cold differ and when the change began. We assess the private installation and explain any utility referral or repair findings.

faq.question: Will a booster pump fix every low-pressure problem?
faq.answer: No. The cause and supply conditions must be established first. Do not assume that installing a pump or altering a valve is appropriate or authorised for the property.

faq.question: Can a repair visit also include a replacement fitting I have chosen?
faq.answer: Ask about both tasks when booking and provide product information if available. The team confirms compatibility and the installation scope before agreement; the original repair request does not automatically include a supplied product.

faq.question: What should a Western Suburbs lighting repair request include?
faq.answer: Include the affected fitting or outlet, property address and a description of what changed.

faq.question: Can fixture and electrical repairs be requested together?
faq.answer: Yes. List each issue separately so it can be assessed as a distinct repair request.
